nodes.title: Annotating a 3D model parked on an ArUco board - and measuring it
widgets_values:
THE POSE (top row, the same head as 45)
'CV ArUco Detect Markers' finds every DICT_6X6_250 marker; 'CV ArUco Board Pose (Average)' averages the per-marker IPPE_SQUARE solutions into one board pose; 'CV Camera Matrix' supplies approximate intrinsics (fx = fy = image width, principal point = centre) - no calibration session. 'marker_length' is what makes the whole graph METRIC: it is the printed edge of one marker, and the tvec (and everything projected against it) comes back in those units. Type 40 mm and the numbers are millimetres - including the one drawn on the overlay. ONE Float node drives it AND the model's scale, so the truck stays 4.87 marker edges long whatever the board actually measures. 'CV Preview 3D (Calibrated Camera)' then composites the truck onto the photo through that exact projection.

ONE PLACEMENT, BOTH LANES
'CV 3D Object Transform' is what keeps the render and the geometry from drifting apart: its 'object_transform' string stands the model up for the VIEWER, and its 4x4 'matrix' moves the MESH ('CV Mesh From 3D Model') and the anchors the same way. Set its 'space' to whatever 'CV Mesh From 3D Model'.axis_convention says - both are OpenCV here - and type the numbers in that space. (A pure 'model_up' turn is the one case where the two spaces agree: conjugating a rotation about X by the 180 deg roll about X between them leaves it unchanged. Any y/z translation or rotation does NOT survive a mismatched dropdown.)

nodes.title: Surface tolerance for the depth test (mm)
LANE 1 - click the MODEL (callouts)
widgets_values: 'CV Annotate Points On Model' is a plain orbit viewer: run the graph once, spin the truck, click its surface. No pose and no lens, because you are pointing at GEOMETRY - the picks come back in the model's own frame, which is what makes them ride the object. 'CV Annotate Model' projects them through the board pose and compares each one's depth against the rasterized surface, so anchors on the far side come back as NaN and the drawing nodes skip them while the labels keep their numbers. The switch turns the depth test off by handing the blueprint a wall at 2048 instead of the real depth ('CV ZeroStride Like') - flip it and the far-side captions reappear through the bodywork. Its 'depth_tolerance' is in SCENE UNITS and therefore has to move with them: the blueprint's own 0.02 suits a scene whose unit is ~1, and at 1 mm per unit it is tighter than the surface's own slope across one pixel, so every near-side caption disappears with it. 0.8 mm here - 2% of a marker edge.

nodes.title: LANE 2 - click the FOOTAGE (measurement), and failure tolerance
widgets_values:
'CV Annotate Points' is the other authoring end: click the RENDER. 'CV Pick Point On Mesh' turns each clicked pixel into a point in the model's frame (rasterize the posed mesh -> read the depth under the click -> unproject -> inverse pose), and 'CV Draw 3D Measurement' puts a dimension line back on the frame, captioned with the distance BETWEEN THE 3D POINTS - not the pixel span of the line it draws. Because the pose is already metric, that caption is MILLIMETRES straight off the board: 178.11 mm bumper to bumper, and THE SCALE COMES FROM THE PRINTED TARGET, not from the model file. (That is the thing the same blueprint in 96 cannot do: there the only clickable geometry is a model whose dimensions the graph already owns, so its number is a round-trip self-check.) Click somewhere off the truck and that point reads valid = 0.

FAILURE TOLERANCE
A photo without markers gives found = false and a zero pose; the viewer bridge falls back to a frontal default, the picks come back invalid and the distance comes back NaN - and the graph still runs to the end, because nothing downstream does arithmetic on it. (Do not put core's 'Math Expression' on that FLOAT to rescale it: it RAISES on a non-finite result, so one stray click would halt the run. Scale the POSE instead, which is what marker_length is for.)

The GLB must sit in ComfyUI/input/3d/MilkTruck.glb (copy it from example_inputs/, see sources.txt).
